spec.name: ad-hoc-delegation
spec.intent:
Checkout /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus. Census @e74f0458 (source identical to d96cede3; only records moved since); re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize `architect role` where it is still unrealized: the routing discipline (a unit reaches the architect only as a name, and it routes names, never a spec it wrote) binds the work of realizing the design, from shard to plan to whole; an ad hoc request from the operator outside that work, such as a comparison, an audit or a question, the architect may hand to whichever role or agent fits it, in its own words. Today the purview guard refuses such a dispatch: the operator saw it refuse an ad hoc comparison of the installed workflow against the design, twice, to an assayer, because the architect's `## Role` and the guard's rubric read every self-worded dispatch as a spec.
CHANGE. (1) packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/architect.ts, the `## Role` every architect holder projects and the purview judge quotes: the `reserves` `dispatch` and the routing lines state that route-by-name binds units of the loop, and that an ad hoc request outside the loop is dispatched to any role or agent that fits it, in the architect's own words (rectified, never the operator's literal words). Also correct the delegation line `⟨gate · merge · state-record · commit ⟨merge · record⟩⟩ ↦ integrator`: recording plan state (bind, active, completed, close) is the planner's; the integrator combines, runs the whole check and commits records (finding 'architect role still hands plan-state records to the integrator').
(2) packages/canon/src/dimensions/actions/delegation.ts: scope `dispatch ↦ name ⟨address ¬ spec(dispatcher-written)⟩` to units of the loop and admit an ad hoc dispatch in the dispatcher's own words; keep every clause reader-reach.test.ts matches (`return ↦ σ*`, `¬long-form-prose`, `human-project ↾ carried-deliverable`, no `ρ=`) and the commit clause.
(3) packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts: the header comment, `residue`, the rubric (the DISPATCH codomain paragraph, 'What to BLOCK', 'What to PASS') and the denial `feedback` pass a dispatch the holder's own contract admits in its own words outside the loop, and keep blocking a dispatch carrying a spec the dispatcher wrote for a unit of the loop and one transcribing the operator's literal words. The rubric still carries no role text and names no agent; the law stays the holder's projected `## Role`. Regenerate packages/canon/targets/guardrail/purview-guardrail.sh and purview-judge-prompt.md with `pnpm canon:project:targets`; no other targets file may change. Change packages/canon/test/purview-guardrail.test.ts only where it breaks.
(4) packages/canon/src/agents/architect.ts, kino.ts, mav.ts, nico.ts and packages/canon/src/roles/architect.ts: no description, archetype or comment says every dispatch is a unit name; where one states the routing it admits the ad hoc exception. The comments at agents/mav.ts:6 and agents/nico.ts:17 spell the retired anchor `architect position`; they say `architect role`.
(5) .changeset/ad-hoc-delegation.md (@cratylus/canon minor). docs/role.md is not this unit's (a disposition record, owned in this plan by integration-line, which also re-spells its one `architect position`). No new test file. The stance guard's dispatch-echo check already passes a substantive dispatch in the dispatcher's own words; leave it.
accept: RIG (every projection leg): T=$(mktemp -d); from cwd /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus run `pnpm build`, then `pnpm exec cratylus project --harness claude --out $T`; both exit 0. The session text of an agent h is $T/agents/<h>.md whole (front matter and hooks included), followed by each skill of its `skills:` list in order as $T/skills/<s>/SKILL.md with its front matter stripped. Print the `## Role` section of $T/agents/architect.md: it states the ad hoc exception, and `state-record` is not routed to the integrator (census: `state-record` occurs once in that section, in the integrator route).

LIVE JUDGE, before and after. Drive the projected purview-guardrail.sh with a PreToolUse payload built as test/purview-guardrail.test.ts's rig builds one (a persona scope whose stance manifest names architect, the projected agents/architect.md, tool_name Task), with no STANCE_* variable set, so the real judge (stance-judge.sh: claude -p, haiku) scores it. P1, subagent_type assayer, an ad hoc request in the architect's own words naming no unit: 'Compare the workflow installed on this host (agents, skills, hooks) with the design as cratylus design show prints it, and report each place they disagree, naming the concept.' P2, subagent_type implementer, a spec the architect wrote for a unit of the loop: 'Unit unit-ledger of plan loop-ledger: in packages/runtime/src/capabilities/plan/unit.ts add a land verb that records the commit, and write its tests.' Run each 3 times on the tree at e74f0458 and 3 times after the change; print every stdout. After: P1 allowed 3 of 3, P2 denied 3 of 3. Before: P1 denied at least once (the operator saw 2 of 2).
`git grep -n 'architect position' -- packages/canon/src` prints nothing (census 2: agents/mav.ts:6, agents/nico.ts:17).

COLD READ. For each of architect, mav, kino and nico, give its session text (RIG) with no other context and no tools, to anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 and anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 with this prompt verbatim: 'Below is the complete definition of an AI agent and the skills loaded into it at session start. Answer from this text alone, quoting the lines that decide each answer, with YES, NO or UNCLEAR where a question asks yes or no. (a) Outside any plan, the operator asks it to compare the installed workflow with the design. May it hand that request to an assayer, or to any other agent that fits, written in its own words? (b) While a plan is bound, may it hand an implementer instructions it wrote itself for a unit of that plan, instead of the unit name? (c) May it pass the operator’s literal words to a delegate as the delegate’s instructions? (d) Does it itself build, run checks, commit, merge, or read a unit, a spec, a diff or an implementer’s account? (e) Who records that a unit is active or completed, or that a plan is closed?' Every read answers (a) YES, (b) NO, (c) NO, (d) NO, (e) the planner, not the integrator. Save each answer under /tmp/loop-ledger-cold-read/ad-hoc-delegation/ and print the (a)-(e) lines.

Green: `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon exec vitest run test/purview-guardrail.test.ts test/reader-reach.test.ts test/reader-density.test.ts test/structural-parsimony.test.ts test/null-dimension.test.ts test/projection-stability.test.ts test/cratylism.test.ts test/skill-hook-cap.test.ts` and `pnpm typecheck` exit 0; after the commit, `pnpm canon:project:targets` leaves `git status --porcelain packages/canon/targets` empty.
